intro: Verbs that change their meaning when they take me, te, se.
p.irse.consejo: «Ir» is to go to a place; «irse» is to leave it: «me voy». It is irregular: «me voy», «te vas».
p.quedarse.consejo: «Quedarse» is not leaving: «me quedo en casa». With «quedar» the meaning changes.
p.quedar.glosa: to arrange to meet; to be left
p.quedar.consejo: «Quedar con alguien» is to arrange to meet: «he quedado con Ana». Also: «quedan dos».
p.dormirse.consejo: «Dormir» is to be asleep; «dormirse» is to fall asleep: «me dormí en el metro».
p.acordarse de.consejo: Always with «de»: «me acuerdo de ti». Without «se», «acordar» is to agree.
p.parecerse a.consejo: Always with «a»: «se parece a su madre». «Parecer» without «se» is «to seem».
p.llevarse bien.consejo: You say «llevarse bien con alguien»: «nos llevamos muy bien». The opposite is «llevarse mal».
p.comerse.consejo: With «se» you eat it all: «se comió la tarta». It needs a whole amount.
p.despedirse de.consejo: You say «despedirse de alguien»: «me despido de ti». It is pronominal.
p.despedir.glosa: to dismiss, to sack; to see off
p.despedir.consejo: «Lo despidieron» means he lost his job. Do not confuse it with «despedirse».
p.negarse a.consejo: It goes with «a» + infinitive: «se niega a salir». «Negar» without «se» is to say it is not true.
p.rato.consejo: You say «un rato». The initial r sounds strong: RRA-to.
b1.texto:
- **ir** is to go somewhere; **irse** is to leave: voy al cine; **me voy**.
- **dormir** is to sleep; **dormirse** is to fall asleep.
- **quedar** is to arrange to meet, or to be left (quedan dos); **quedarse** is to stay.
- **acordar** is to agree; **acordarse de** is to remember.
- **parecer** is to seem; **parecerse a** is to look like.
- **llevar** is to carry or wear; **llevarse** is to take away, and **llevarse bien** is to get on well.
- **despedir** is to sack; **despedirse** is to say goodbye.
- **negar** is to deny; **negarse a** is to refuse.
- **encontrar** is to find; **encontrarse** is to meet, or to feel.

With eating, drinking and reading, **se** shows that a whole amount is finished: **se comió** toda la tarta; **me leí** el libro en un día. It needs a definite amount: como pan, but **me comí** el pan.
b2.f3.texto: I've arranged to meet my brother at nine.
b2.f4.texto: Is he the one who looks so much like you?
b2.f6.texto: Yesterday he ate up my whole dinner.
b2.f7.texto: Don't fall asleep on the underground, it's late.
b4.texto:
**Many verbs change meaning with «se»:**

- ir → irse (to leave)
- dormir → dormirse (to fall asleep)
- quedar (to meet) → quedarse (to stay)
- acordar (to agree) → acordarse de (to remember)
- parecer → parecerse a (to look like)
- despedir (to sack) → despedirse de (to say goodbye)
- negar → negarse a (to refuse)

With eating, drinking and reading verbs, «se» shows that the whole amount is finished.
b5.f0.texto: The party fades little by little in the garden of the house.
b5.f1.texto: The candles leave a trail of warm wax on the table.
b5.f2.texto: A guest falls asleep in the hammock with his hat over his face.
b5.f3.texto: Another eats up the last piece of cake with his eyes closed.
b5.f4.texto: The night smells of cut grass and wood smoke.
b5.f5.texto: Paula remembers the first afternoon in that house.
b5.f6.texto: She says goodbye to the neighbours with a long hug.
b5.f7.texto: The dog of the house refuses to let go of its ball.
b5.f8.texto: Paula stays a while at the door, with the light of the hallway at her back.
b5.f9.texto: Then she goes off along the empty street under a sky full of stars.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «irse» is leaving a place, «me voy».
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Te voy» does not agree with «voy», which is first person.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Le» is not a reflexive pronoun for «irse».
b6.pregunta: Leaving a place: choose the pronoun.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «quedar con» is to arrange a meeting.
b7.o1: me he quedado en casa con Ana
b7.o1.refuerzo: That would be «me he quedado con Ana», with «me».
b8.frase: No te duermas en el metro
b8.traduccion: Don't fall asleep on the underground
b9.o1.refuerzo: «De» is not used with «parecerse»; «a» is used.
b11.o2.refuerzo: Only one: the other one only said goodbye.
b11.pregunta: In «lo despidieron» and «se despidió», who lost his job?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «se» shows he finished the whole amount.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Le» would be «to him» or «to her»; it does not mark the amount.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Lo» cannot replace «la tarta», which is feminine.
b12.pregunta: Show that the whole cake was finished.
p.quédate.consejo: Imperative of «quedarse», to stay. The stress is on KE: KE-da-te.
p.duermas.consejo: Subjunctive of «dormir», to sleep. The ue is a diphthong: DUER-mas.
p.despido.consejo: From «despedirse», to say goodbye. Stress on PI: des-PI-do.
p.despidieron.consejo: Past tense of «despedir», to dismiss from work. The ie is a diphthong.
p.despidió.consejo: Past tense of «despedirse», to say goodbye. The ió is a diphthong.
p.niega.consejo: From «negar», to deny. The ie is a diphthong: NIE-ga.
p.rastro.consejo: Masculine, «el rastro». The rr sound is strong at the start: RAS-tro.
p.hamaca.consejo: Feminine, «la hamaca». The h is silent. Stress on MA.
p.cortada.consejo: Feminine participle of «cortar», to cut. Stress on TA.
p.leña.consejo: Feminine, «la leña». The ñ sounds ny. Stress on LE.
p.acuerda.consejo: From «acordarse», to remember. The ue is a diphthong: a-KUER-da.
p.citado.consejo: Participle of «citar», to arrange to meet. The c before i is th in Spain.
